solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Those players who’ve scored might mark? (8)

definitions.text: Those players who’ve scored might mark?

blocks.note: the surface wants sportsmen who have found the net; the setter means seducers who have made a conquest
not a scoresheet but a notch cut in the wooden frame of a bed, one per conquest

annotation.surface: Footballers who have found the net chalk up their goals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Players' and 'scored' read as sport, but a player is a seducer and scoring is a conquest; the old boast is a notch on the bedpost.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a lothario is said to put notches on his bedpost, so bedposts are what such players mark.

entries.clue: Exceptionally big hit by Queen in the 70s (6)

blocks.note: a bump is a knock or hit
ER = Elizabeth Regina, who was on the throne through the 1970s

annotation.surface: Queen, the rock band, had a massive chart hit in the seventies.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at Freddie Mercury's band, formed in 1970; the wordplay wants the monarch reigning then.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective sense, as in a bumper crop or bumper year, one far larger than usual.

entries.clue: I had to return Spider? Most awful! (6)

indicators.note: returning sends I'D back the way it came, giving DI

blocks.note: I had = I'D
in snooker a spider is a raised rest for the cue

annotation.surface: Someone forced to bring back a spider finds it the worst thing ever.
annotation.walkthrough: Spider is not the creature but a snooker rest, a cue support with long legs that lets the player bridge over other balls.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the superlative of dire, dreadful, matching 'most awful'.

entries.clue: Exactly how one might first judge a wine? (2,3,4)

definitions.text: how one might first judge a wine

blocks.note: precisely, spot on, as a punctual arrival or a bet placed to win

blocks.clueFragment: how one might first judge a wine
blocks.note: a taster smells a wine's aroma before sipping

annotation.surface: A wine buff explains precisely how to assess a bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: A wine's 'nose' is its aroma, the first thing a taster assesses before drinking.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for precisely, plus the literal sense of assessing wine by its smell.

entries.clue: Mating: an idea gone over repeatedly (4,3,5)

indicators.note: letters that have been gone over are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: Someone keeps returning to the thought of mating, over and over.
annotation.walkthrough: The colon is surface punctuation only; the twelve letters of 'Mating an idea' make the whole answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning on many occasions, over and over.

entries.clue: Unit repel charge by half-destroyed sector (6)

indicators.note: to repel is to drive back, so RAP is sent backwards
half of SECTOR is knocked out, leaving SEC

blocks.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'
the first half of the word, its first three of six letters

annotation.surface: A military unit fights off an attack on a sector already half in ruins.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a battle, but 'Unit' is the definition, a measure of distance, and 'repel' turns a word around rather than fighting anyone.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: an astronomical unit of distance, about 3.26 light years.

entries.clue: I love to visit old fighter in Mayo (5)

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so IO sits within ALI

blocks.note: as printed
love = O, the zero in tennis scoring
Muhammad Ali, the retired boxer

annotation.surface: Someone longs to call on a veteran fighter in County Mayo, Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: Mayo reads as the Irish county but is short for mayonnaise.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a garlic mayonnaise from Provence, so a kind of mayo.

entries.clue: Trieste ward sensibly embraces supervisors (8)
Tory ministers’ debates (8)

blocks.note: Con = Conservative
ministers to = tends; the apostrophe-s is read as 'ministers is'

annotation.surface: Conservative government ministers hold their debates.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ministers' is a verb, as in ministering to the sick, not members of a cabinet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to contend is to argue a point, to debate.

entries.clue: Issue with one animal brought over by sea (8)

indicators.note: brought over means turned back to front, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: to issue is to emit
I = one, the Roman numeral
a ram, male sheep

annotation.surface: A creature is shipped across the water.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an animal on a ferry; all three pieces are turned round together, not one at a time.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: maritime means connected with or carried on by sea.

entries.clue: Religious work interrupted by English national (6)

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so E breaks into KORAN

blocks.note: the Koran, Islam's holy book
E = English

annotation.surface: An English citizen disrupts someone reading a holy book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun here, a citizen of a country.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a citizen of Korea is one kind of national.

entries.clue: Hint a nude oaf dances well (12)

indicators.note: the letters move around like dancers

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A suggestion that a naked lout is a good dancer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well' sits at the end looking like an adverb to 'dances'; it is a noun, a spring of water.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fountainhead is a spring or source of water.

entries.clue: Take action with nurse to get result (5)

blocks.note: EN = Enrolled Nurse
take (legal) action = sue

annotation.surface: Someone takes a nurse to court in hope of an outcome.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' lets the nurse go first. An Enrolled Nurse is a British nursing grade.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to ensue is to follow as a consequence.

entries.clue: Detest moderate old minister punches (9)

indicators.note: ABATE punches a hole and takes O MIN inside

blocks.note: to abate is to lessen or moderate
O = old
Min = minister

annotation.surface: A politician hates the sight of a moderate former minister who lashes out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Punches' reads as violence, but it signals one word being pierced by others.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to loathe intensely, to detest.

entries.clue: How one can describe Pinocchio or Dopey (12)

definitions.text: How one can describe Pinocchio or Dopey

blocks.note: the puppet boy carved by Geppetto, so literally made of timber
the dimmest of Snow White's seven dwarfs, so figuratively thick

annotation.surface: A quiz about Disney characters: the puppet boy and the silliest dwarf.
annotation.walkthrough: One word serves both characters, literally for the puppet and figuratively for the dwarf.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal and an idiomatic sense: made of wood above the neck, and stupid.

entries.clue: Conductor chosen for ultimately lyrical work (9)

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of 'for'

blocks.note: elect = chosen, as in 'the president elect'
last letter of 'for'
an ode is a lyric poem

annotation.surface: An orchestra's conductor has been picked for a piece of lyrical music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' paints a maestro with a baton; it means something that conducts electricity.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a solid conductor through which current enters or leaves a circuit.

entries.clue: Climber training in balmy area (5,3)

blocks.note: balmy air is sweet and fragrant
PE = physical education
A = area

annotation.surface: A mountaineer trains somewhere with a warm climate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a fragrant garden plant that climbs by tendrils.

entries.clue: Ball crossed by agile men onto level pitch (8)

indicators.note: the ball has the other letters crossing around it
agile letters move nimbly into a new order

blocks.note: rearranged; the ball goes in after the third letter
a ball is round, like O

annotation.surface: Nimble players run on to a flat pitch, the ball crossed to them.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is sport, with a ball crossed onto a level pitch; here 'pitch' is musical.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a single unvarying tone, one level of pitch.

entries.clue: Do wrong or evade crafty type? (4,8)

indicators.note: to do letters is to fix or arrange them anew, as a hairdo arranges hair

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A sly character is tempted to sin or dodge the rules.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do wrong' looks like one phrase, but 'Do' is the instruction; 'crafty type' is a craftsman, with the question mark flagging the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: someone who practises a craft is literally crafty, not cunning.

entries.clue: Depression etched into a smiling face? (6)

definitions.text: Depression etched into a smiling face?

blocks.note: the surface wants low mood; the setter means a small physical hollow
the hollow that appears in the cheek when someone smiles

annotation.surface: Sadness hidden behind a cheerful expression.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as low mood, the opposite of a smile, but it is a physical dent.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a small hollow in the cheek, most visible when smiling.

entries.clue: Trumpets Lionel and Tony possibly picked up (6)

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: Lionel Blair, the dancer and TV host, and Tony Blair, the Prime Minister

annotation.surface: Two famous men are overheard sounding off.
annotation.walkthrough: Lionel Blair was a British entertainer; with Tony Blair he makes two of a surname. 'Possibly' says they are examples.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to trumpet is to sound loudly.

entries.clue: Slow progress in uprising repels resistance (9)

indicators.note: the uprising pushes R away, dropping it

blocks.note: an uprising is a revolution
R = resistance, the physics symbol; removed

annotation.surface: A rebellion makes little headway against the resistance.
annotation.walkthrough: Taking one letter off the sudden upheaval leaves its gradual opposite.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gradual development as opposed to sudden change.

entries.clue: Marry one without trace of duplicity (5)

indicators.note: without means lacking, so D is taken away
a trace is just the first bit, D

blocks.note: being one = joined together, as a couple are
first letter of 'duplicity'; removed

annotation.surface: Wed someone utterly honest, with no hint of deceit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' is not the number but the adjective for a joined pair.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to marry is to join two people together.

entries.clue: Examination of pain in the neck (5)

blocks.note: a test, as of a new drug
a nuisance, a trying person

annotation.surface: A doctor looks at a patient's stiff neck.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is medical; both halves are senses of one word, a test and an annoyance.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one noun: a test, and something or someone trying.

entries.clue: Advantage of entering river-flooded mine (6)

indicators.note: to enter is to go in, so 'of' goes inside the flooded mine
the river pours into the mine, so R goes inside PIT

blocks.note: R = river
as printed
a pit is a coal mine

annotation.surface: Someone gains from getting into a mine swamped by a river.
annotation.walkthrough: There are two insertions, and the second slots in after the first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a gain or benefit, an advantage.

entries.clue: Where old man’s SEAT is picked up for crook? (5,3)

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: your dad's seat, his backside, is beneath Pa

annotation.surface: A question about where a Spanish SEAT car belongs to a thief.
annotation.walkthrough: SEAT is capitalised to look like the Spanish car maker; it is the bottom. Old man = Pa. In non-rhotic British speech PA and PAR sound alike.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Australian slang crook means ill, off colour.

entries.clue: Parrot or full-sized old primates (6)

indicators.note: OR, other ranks, is expanded to its full meaning, MEN

blocks.note: to parrot is to ape, copy
OR = other ranks, i.e. ordinary soldiers

annotation.surface: A question of whether a parrot or large, elderly monkeys come first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like the conjunction, but it is OR, other ranks; 'full-sized' asks for what that stands for.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: early hominids, primitive primates of long ago.

entries.clue: Python with tongue maybe going after sloth (8)

blocks.note: Eric Idle of Monty Python
a ness is a headland, a tongue of land

annotation.surface: A python flicking its tongue goes hunting a sloth.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a snake hunting a slow animal, but Python is the comedy troupe and sloth is laziness.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sloth, one of the seven deadly sins, is laziness.
